_what: Hand-read revenue lines and group structure, one entry per security. A security is in this file only because the issuer's own report was opened and read. Everything else is derived from the statements the terminal holds, or marked not on file, by build_business_model.py.

source.doc: Safaricom Plc Annual Report and Financial Statements 2026
source.basis: the issuer's own audited annual report, read page by page
source.pageNote: Page numbers are the ones printed in the report, not PDF positions.

lines.name: M-PESA
lines.note: Note 5(a) Revenue from contracts with customers
lines.what: Mobile money. A graduated tariff on every deposit, transfer and withdrawal, commission on Lipa Na M-PESA and Pochi La Biashara merchant payments, and fees on remittances. Transactions up to KShs 100, or KShs 200 at a merchant, are free under the Kadogo tariff. Note 2(f), page 163.

lines.name: Mobile data
lines.note: Note 5(a) Revenue from contracts with customers
lines.what: Internet bundles sold in advance, hourly to monthly, plus pay as you go. The bundle is deferred on purchase and becomes revenue on the earlier of usage or expiry. Note 2(f), page 162.

lines.name: Voice
lines.note: Note 5(a) Revenue from contracts with customers
lines.what: Calls. Prepay at KShs 4.67 a minute peak and KShs 2.40 off peak, recognised on usage; postpay billed monthly. Note 2(f), page 161.

lines.name: Fixed data
lines.note: Note 5(a) Revenue from contracts with customers
lines.what: Home and business fibre, FTTH and FTTB, priced on contracted bandwidth, charged upfront for 7 or 30 days and spread over the subscription. Note 2(f), page 162.

lines.name: Messaging
lines.note: Note 5(a) Revenue from contracts with customers
lines.what: SMS at KShs 1.20 a message on net and off net, cheaper in a bundle; revenue on the earlier of usage or bundle expiry. Note 2(f), page 162.

lines.name: Interconnect
lines.note: Note 5(a) Revenue from contracts with customers
lines.what: What other networks pay Safaricom when their customers' calls terminate on its network, under interconnect agreements with local and foreign partners. Note 2(f), page 161.

lines.name: Mobile incoming
lines.note: Note 5(a) Revenue from contracts with customers
lines.what: Calls and messages arriving from abroad, and visitors roaming on the network billed to their home operator. Note 2(f), page 162.

lines.name: Other services
lines.note: Note 5(a) Revenue from contracts with customers
lines.what: Okoa Jahazi emergency airtime fees, roaming revenue and bulk SMS, as the note itself defines the line.

lines.name: Handset
lines.note: Note 5(a) Revenue from contracts with customers
lines.what: Phones and devices sold outright or over the term of a service agreement.

lines.name: Connection
lines.note: Note 5(a) Revenue from contracts with customers
lines.what: Connection charges on new lines and fixed line installations.

lines.name: Site rental
lines.what: Rent from other operators and tenants on Safaricom's own tower and mast sites.

lines.name: Miscellaneous income
lines.what: Cash discounts received from vendors and non-recurring revenue from partnership agreements, as the note defines it.

lines.name: Loss on disposal of property and equipment
lines.what: A disposal result, not a trading line. It sits inside the reported revenue total, so it is shown rather than hidden.

segments.name: Kenya
segments.what: The licensed Kenyan network, M-PESA and the fixed business.

segments.name: Ethiopia
segments.what: Safaricom Telecommunications Ethiopia Plc, reached through Vodafamily Ethiopia Holding and Global Partnership for Ethiopia. It lost KShs 47,148.4Mn after tax in the year, Note 23(a) page 215.

segments.name: Inter-segment elimination
segments.what: Trade between the two segments, removed so nothing is counted twice.

revenue.note: The income statement's revenue line, KShs 427,559.1Mn, is Note 5(a) plus Note 5(b): 420,992.1 from contracts with customers and 6,567.0 from other sources.
revenue.headline: Mobile money is the biggest line and still growing: M-PESA alone is KShs 182.7 billion of KShs 427.6 billion, ahead of mobile data at 92.9 and voice at 84.8. Voice, once the whole business, is now third.

entities.name: Digifarm Kenya Limited
entities.note: Note 23(a) Investment in subsidiaries
entities.what: Agribusiness technology for Kenyan farmers: inputs, credit, extension advice and a route to buyers. Share capital KShs 100,000.

entities.name: Safaricom Insurance Agency Limited
entities.note: Note 23(a) Investment in subsidiaries
entities.what: Licensed in May 2024 as an insurance intermediary: health, motor, business, travel and accident cover co-created with insurers.

entities.name: M-PESA Holding Co. Limited
entities.note: Note 23(a) Investment in subsidiaries
entities.what: The licensed payment provider, bought from Vodafone International Holdings BV for one dollar after the July 2023 AGM. It holds customer funds in trust and its results are not consolidated.

entities.name: Safaricom Spark Fund Company Limited by Guarantee
entities.note: Note 32 Related party transactions, percentage of interest held
entities.what: New in the year; it was not in the 2025 table.

entities.name: Safaricom Foundation
entities.note: Note 32 Related party transactions, percentage of interest held
entities.what: A public charitable trust declared on 14 August 2003, domiciled in Kenya. The table prints no percentage against it.

entities.name: Vodafamily Ethiopia Holding Company Limited
entities.note: Note 23(a) Investment in subsidiaries
entities.what: Incorporated in England and Wales, run from London. The table reads 90% less one share. Almost all of the KShs 147,807.4Mn carrying value of the subsidiaries sits here.

entities.name: Global Partnership for Ethiopia B.V
entities.note: Note 32 Related party transactions, percentage of interest held
entities.what: A Dutch company held with Vodacom, Sumitomo, British International Investment and the IFC, who together hold 45.83% of the Ethiopian venture.

entities.note: Note 32 Related party transactions, percentage of interest held

entities.note: Note 32 Related party transactions, percentage of interest held

entities.name: The East African Marine System Limited (TEAMS)
entities.note: Note 23(b) Investment in associates and joint venture
entities.what: Submarine fibre optic cable capacity. Kenyan, unquoted, and small: its whole nine month revenue was KShs 239.7Mn.

entities.name: East Africa Device Assembly Kenya Limited (EADAK)
entities.note: Note 23(b) Investment in associates and joint venture
entities.what: Mobile phone assembly in Kenya, with other shareholders. It paid the group KShs 220.6Mn of profit share this year.

entities.name: Circle Gas Limited
entities.note: Note 32 Related party transactions, percentage of interest held
entities.what: Named in the related party note. Note 23(b) prints no separate carrying amount for it.

entities.name: M-PESA Africa Limited
entities.note: Note 23(b) Investment in associates and joint venture
entities.what: A fifty fifty venture with Vodacom holding the M-PESA brand and platform across Africa, bought from Vodafone in March 2020. It charges Safaricom a monthly fee of 2% of M-PESA transaction revenue, and owns K2019102008 South Africa Proprietary Limited outright.

group.note: Percentages are the ones printed in Note 32. Where an entity is held through another the chain is drawn, with the report's own indirect percentage beside it.
